definitions.explanation: A woman who is one's spouse's older sister, or one's older stepsister through a parent's remarriage. A formal term used in legal and written contexts.

examples.japanese: {義姉|ぎし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
{義姉|ぎし}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧⟦{以来|いらい}→以来：01831_irai⟧⟦ずっと→ずっと：00912_zutto⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: I've been on good terms with my sister-in-law ever since we married.

examples.japanese: {義姉|ぎし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出産|しゅっさん}した→出産する：26987_shussansuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦お{祝|いわ}い→お祝い：01339_oiwai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}った→贈る：09862_okuru⟧。
examples.english: My sister-in-law gave birth, so I sent a gift to celebrate.

notes:
USAGE:
{義姉|ぎし} is the formal/written form. In speech, ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧ or お{義姉|ねえ}さん are more natural. The character {義|ぎ} indicates a relationship through marriage rather than blood.
Also read as ぎし in compounds. In casual speech, people may say お{義姉|ねえ}さん to address their sister-in-law directly.

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- ⟦{義妹|ぎまい}→義妹：18404_gimai⟧: younger sister-in-law
- ⟦{義兄|ぎけい}→義兄：15784_gikei⟧: older brother-in-law
- ⟦{義弟|ぎてい}→義弟：13981_gitei⟧: younger brother-in-law
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧: sister-in-law (conversational form)
